claims: USDC end-of-period circulation was USD 73.269B; average circulation USD 76.524B; Q2 onchain transaction volume USD 14.8T.

Q2 USDC minted through Circle Mint was USD 83.004B and redeemed USD 86.784B, net gross-flow difference -USD 3.780B; H1 minted USD 156.543B and redeemed USD 158.540B, net difference -USD 1.997B. These are Circle Mint customer flows, not a complete chain-wide transfer ledger.
USDC stablecoin market share was 27% at quarter end; meaningful wallets were 7.01M, defined as wallets holding more than USD 10 and not unique end-users.
Circle's Q2 reserve return rate was 3.5%, down from 4.1% in Q2 2025.

Circle said a 25.2% increase in average daily USDC in circulation added approximately USD 147.4M to Q2 reserve income, while a 66-basis-point decline in average yields, reflecting U.S. Federal Reserve rate actions, reduced reserve income by approximately USD 113.9M.

Coinbase allocations under the Collaboration Agreement depend on USDC held on Coinbase after issuer retention and half of remaining broader ecosystem growth after approved third-party participant payments.
Circle incurred USD 324.6M of distribution costs in connection with Coinbase agreements in Q2 and USD 655.3M in H1.

Circle said Q2 distribution costs paid to Coinbase decreased USD 7.7M year over year due to a lower Coinbase share of total average USDC on-platform balances, while overall distribution costs increased due to new and existing strategic distribution partnerships.
Q3 2026 stablecoin revenue was USD 306.905M versus USD 324.534M in Q3 2025, a USD 17.629M / 5.4% decline.
Q3 2026 subscription and services revenue was USD 570.238M, 49% of net revenue; stablecoin revenue represented approximately 53.8% of subscription and services revenue.
For the first nine months of 2026, stablecoin revenue was USD 904.487M versus USD 907.485M in the comparable prior-year period.
Coinbase said higher average USDC balances in its products added USD 84.6M to year-to-date stablecoin revenue, while lower average interest rates reduced it by USD 52.8M.
Coinbase's Q3 2026 filing identifies stablecoin revenue as sensitive to USDC balances and interest rates.
Average USDC held in Coinbase products reached USD 22B in Q3 2026, approximately 30% of average USDC market capitalization, and increased 49% year over year.
Coinbase reported 10.7% crypto trading-volume market share, versus 5.6% in Q3 2025, and assets on platform equal to 12.5% of total crypto market capitalization.

Coinbase reported 179% compound annual growth in crypto derivatives trading volume over the prior two years and said its INTX/Deribit integration was completed in October; it expected some near-term volume volatility while participants adjusted.
Coinbase reported subscription and services at 49% of net revenue and prediction-market annualized revenue above USD 200M.

hypotheses.claim: Circle and Coinbase have a mutually reinforcing but rate-sensitive USDC distribution model.
support: Circle's contract allocates economics partly by Coinbase-held USDC balances and broader ecosystem growth.
Circle paid USD 324.6M Q2 / USD 655.3M H1 distribution costs in connection with Coinbase agreements.
Coinbase held USD 22B average USDC in Q3 and generated USD 306.905M stablecoin revenue.
Both Circle and Coinbase filings describe interest-rate sensitivity.
counterevidence: Circle's Q2 reserve income still grew 5.3% year over year as higher circulation offset lower yields.
Coinbase's Q3 stablecoin revenue declined only 5.4% year over year, while average USDC balances grew 49%.
Circle also distributes through Binance and other approved partners; Coinbase is significant but not exclusive.
hypotheses.confidence: strongly supported for economic linkage; price-market effect unquantified

hypotheses.claim: Lower U.S. rates can compress stablecoin economics even when USDC balances grow, increasing the incentive to expand distribution, onchain payments and agentic use cases.
support: Circle attributes a USD 113.9M Q2 reserve-income headwind to a 66bp decline in average yields, partly offset by USD 147.4M from higher average USDC circulation.
Coinbase's SEC filing records stablecoin revenue gains from higher USDC balances and offsets from lower average rates.
Circle Agent Stack and Arc, plus Coinbase stablecoin/agent payments, expand use cases beyond passive balances.
counterevidence: Higher circulation can offset lower yields, and revenue also depends on distribution agreements, other services and transaction volumes.
No direct XRP price response or substitution elasticity has been established.
hypotheses.confidence: strongly supported for business economics; XRP price causality untested

market_implications.confirmed: Circle's USDC and Coinbase's distribution economics are materially connected through explicit contractual allocation rules and reported costs/revenue.
market_implications.inference: The partnership gives Coinbase a large economic incentive to grow USDC balances and ecosystem usage, while Circle bears substantial distribution costs and has incentives to broaden distribution beyond Coinbase.
market_implications.xrp_boundary: This is not evidence of XRP purchases, XRP collateral utilization or an XRP payment share. Stablecoin economics can expand without XRP being the transfer asset.
market_implications.macro_boundary: Rate sensitivity is documented by both issuers; a directional XRP forecast requires point-in-time market data and tested causal features.

next_actions: Track USDC mint/redemption flows, circulation, average reserve yield and platform balances by quarter.
Separate Coinbase USDC balances from Circle's own platform balances and third-party ecosystem balances.
Compare stablecoin revenue sensitivity with Fed policy expectations and U.S. Treasury yields using point-in-time data.
Track Arc and Coinbase agent-payment activity separately from XRPL and RLUSD flows.
Measure any XRP-specific collateral use or bridge volume directly; do not infer it from stablecoin growth.
